Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the note and great call. A couple of specifics from our security team we want clarified before the deep-dive: 

1) Role model: Do you support per-tenant custom roles (we want FinanceAdmin, OpsAnalyst, ReadOnly) or is it RBAC with fixed roles? Can permissions be scoped to resources (dataset or model)?

2) Support access: For break-glass, does support get full tenant-level tokens or time-limited, audited session-based access? Do you require a customer approval flow for each incident?

3) Audit logs & retention: What event types are captured (access, read, write, policy changes) and what are default retention windows? Can we export logs to our SIEM and set retention to 7 years if required?

4) Data residency: We need guarantee that PII and logs for FinTrust accounts in prod will remain in us-east or us-west only. Is cross-region fallback possible and how is data access handled during failover?

If you can send a short doc answering #1–#4, that will help our security team prepare focused questions for the technical deep-dive.

Best,

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers below; I’ve attached a two-page runbook and our most recent SOC2 snapshot for the controls you care about. If anything needs more detail we can walk through in the deep-dive.

1) Role model
- We support a tenant-scoped RBAC model with customizable roles. Customers can define roles and map permissions to resources (models, datasets, routes). We also provide a set of default roles (Admin, Developer, ReadOnly, Support) to accelerate setup.

2) Support access / break-glass
- Support access is time-limited and session-based. We do not issue permanent tenant-wide tokens to support engineers.
- Break-glass flow: customer initiates a request (email or portal), on-call approver triggers a short-lived elevation (typically 1h) that is logged and requires a reason. We also support approval via existing SSO/SAML flows (if you prefer the request to be gated).
- All sessions are recorded in the audit log with the before/after state for config changes.

3) Audit logs & retention
- Event types captured: auth events, API calls (read/write), admin actions (role changes, policy updates), support session start/stop, model inference metadata (no raw prompt storage by default unless configured).
- Default retention: 90 days in the UI, exportable to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/BigQuery), we can support longer retention policies via exports.
- If you need 7-year retention we recommend a regular export to your retention bucket; we can automate exports as part of onboarding.

4) Data residency & failover
- You can pin production workloads to a region (us-east-1 or us-west-2). We support cross-region failover but only operate it per your policy — data movement during failover is audited and we can set restrictions so backups are also region-restricted.

Attachments included:
- support-breakglass-runbook.pdf (2pp) — runbook with steps, approval flow, and sample audit entries.
- SOC2-snapshot-2026Q2.pdf — snapshot of controls in-scope for access controls and logging.

Next steps I recommend:
- Marissa: schedule the 30–45m technical session; invite your security lead + our infra/security engineer.
- Alice: confirm secondary contact and whether you want export automation for long-term retention.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
